A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CD-T research. Their text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including the new Appendix B in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original CD-T experiments on IOI, Greater-than, and Docstring, including runtime, circuit recovery, faithfulness, and appendix circuit analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in Figures 1–2 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the stated pruning scope from newly selected nodes S to the accumulated circuit C, with repeated removal passes until C stops changing. The decomposition equations and relevance metric remain unchanged. Layerwise normalization is retained in Appendix B.1 rather than removed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same IOI, Greater-than, and Docstring tasks, including the same corrupted-input scenarios. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains ACDC and EAP comparisons. Figure 2 retains EAP, random circuits, and manual references, with ACDC still omitted. Appendix A's manual-circuit comparisons are unchanged; EAP-IG remains discussed but unevaluated.

E3.justification: The models, task-specific discovery and evaluation sample counts, metrics, ablation distributions, and 90–99 percentile sweep remain unchanged. V3's general recommendation to average 10–100 inputs adds guidance without revising the experiments' stated protocols.

E4.justification: The mean-versus-zero ablation comparison, circuit-size analysis, random-circuit tests, and Appendix A's IOI heatmaps and circuit case studies are retained. Appendix B adds methodological discussion without a new ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random-circuit repetitions and the same runtime averaging across threshold sweeps. Neither adds seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates. The new input-averaging guidance does not describe additional experimental runs.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 and Appendix A's numerical results are unchanged. V3 adds brief qualitative observations that averaging 10–100 inputs typically yields stable performance (Section 3.3.1) and that contribution distributions vary substantially (Appendix B.1), without new quantitative evaluations.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.2 adds complexity reasoning: decomposition costs comparable to a forward pass, memory below three times a forward pass, and linear scaling with input count and node granularity. The underlying decomposition equations remain unchanged; no new correctness proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about efficient fine-grained discovery, transformer compatibility, 97% average ROC AUC, superiority to random circuits, and full-model faithfulness with fewer nodes. The added code-availability statement concerns reproducibility.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 adds qualifications about finding universally suitable selection heuristics and possible numerical instability. The limitation that circuit discovery does not automatically produce an interpretation moves into Section 3.3.1; concerns about interpretable score scales remain in Appendix A.

D1.justification: V2 promises a future package; v3 states that implementation and reproduction code are available and supplies a repository link. V3 also documents handling of opposite-sign decomposition constituents and explains input averaging. These disclosures do not establish that the experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: The reference lists and substantive positioning relative to contextual decomposition, activation patching, and SAE methods are unchanged. Section 2.2 elaborates the manual effort required by earlier approaches without materially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: The standalone circuit-definition section moves into Section 3.3.1, the algorithm explanation is revised, the limitations discussion is condensed, and Appendix B is added. Most introductory, experimental, and Appendix A prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 expands into a nested-loop display, conference headers are added, and text reflows around the reorganized sections and new appendix. Figures 1–2, appendix heatmaps, and result-table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The repository pointer, expanded pruning description, and Appendix B's implementation and complexity details modestly improve reproducibility and clarity. Quantitative validation is unchanged, and some details remain underspecified, including the constituent chosen for zeroing in the stabilization rule, so the overall gain is limited.
